name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Broadening expressed where broadening is actually happening: a doubled energy sleeve behind a re-escalating Hormuz supply shock, an equal-weight and free-cash-flow value core, a halved gold complex that is losing to a hiking Fed, and a small anti-concentration QQQ short against a 1999-style narrow tape.
reassessment_note: Two things in my strategy of record were falsified this week and I am acting on both. First, I wrote that energy should be trimmed 'as the war premium bleeds out.' The opposite happened: on 2026-09-28 Trump rejected Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and told aides he expects strikes to resume after the November midterms. Brent is ~$105-107 and WTI ~$94, and energy is the top S&P sector in 2026 at roughly +32% YTD. That trim thesis is dead, so I am reversing it and taking energy from 14% to 28% via XLE plus equal-weighted E&P in XOP. Second, my 26% gold complex is fighting the wrong regime. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with 16 of 18 participants expecting another, the 10y is 5.24% and the 30y 5.56% (a 22-year high), the dollar is 101.18, and gold fell 3.19% on 2026-09-28 to ~$4,149 precisely because the oil spike hardened rate-hike bets. Rising real yields plus a firming dollar is the one combination gold cannot win, so GDX and GLD are halved to 14% rather than abandoned, because the same Fed reaction function that is hurting gold is helping energy, which makes the two sleeves genuine diversifiers of each other, and because sell-side 12-18 month targets still cluster at $5,000-6,300. I also cut the 3% ETH debasement tail: it is the same trade as gold, at 35bps a side, in a regime where the Fed is visibly winning the tightening argument. The core broadening expression stays put despite a hostile tape. Breadth has genuinely collapsed, with roughly 60% of S&P names 20%-plus off highs and only 27% above their 50-day while the index sits near a record. That is the anti-broadening regime, but it is also a washed-out setup that Morgan Stanley reads as resolving in either a pullback or a catch-up rally in the laggards. I am the broadening manager and I am not going to capitulate at the point of maximum narrowness, so RSP, COWZ and XLI hold at 40% combined and the QQQ short stays as the explicit anti-concentration tail.

positions.thesis: The single highest-conviction leg and the direct reversal of last week's mistaken trim. Trump's 2026-09-28 rejection of Iran's Hormuz proposal removes the de-escalation path that justified cutting energy, and his stated expectation that strikes resume after the November midterms means the supply risk is not a one-week headline but a structural overhang into year-end. XLE is 91% oil and gas with over 40% in Exxon and Chevron, so it is the cleanest large-cap expression of a crude price that has more than doubled off late-2025 lows. It also serves the mandate directly: energy is a broadening sector, not a mega-cap tech one, and it is leading the S&P while breadth collapses everywhere else. Size 20% because Saudi restoring ~3.5mbpd caps the upside somewhat and a genuine ceasefire would hit this hard, which the 15% stop is there to handle.

The mandate anchor, held at full size into the worst possible tape on purpose. Equal-weight S&P is the purest statement that the index's gains should broaden out of the Mag7, and right now it is losing badly: only 27% of S&P names are above their 50-day and 60% are in 20%-plus drawdowns while the cap-weighted index prints near records. I am holding rather than adding because I do not want to average into a trend that is still running against me, and holding rather than cutting because capitulating on equal-weight at the single most extreme breadth reading of the cycle is how a broadening book turns a drawdown into a permanent loss. The 12% stop is my discipline if the 1999 analogy keeps extending.

Free-cash-flow value is the leg best matched to a higher-for-longer regime, so it gets a small increase from 15%. With the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% and another hike expected, the market's dividing line is between businesses that must refinance at 5.5% and businesses that self-fund from operating cash. COWZ screens directly for the latter, which is why I removed the refinancing-vulnerable small and mid-cap sleeve entirely and did not add it back here. It is also a broadening expression that does not depend on the Fed pivoting, unlike almost everything else that would benefit from breadth repair.

Halved from 16% after a -6.93% week, but deliberately not cut to zero. Miners carry operational leverage in both directions, which is why GDX ran 50% over the trailing year and then gave back this much in days as gold slid to ~$4,149 on hardening rate-hike bets. With real yields rising and the dollar at 101.18, the near-term cycle is against me and an 18% stop respects that. I keep 8% because the same Iran escalation driving my energy sleeve is a live geopolitical bid for gold, because gold is already roughly 25% below its January peak rather than extended, and because every major bank's 12-18 month target sits well above spot. This is a tail holding now, not a thesis leg.

New leg, chosen specifically because it serves the energy call and the broadening mandate at the same time. XOP is an equal-weighted index of 54 US exploration and production companies, so unlike XLE it is not 40% two supermajors, which gives higher beta to the crude price and puts money into the broad middle of the sector rather than its two largest names. It returned about 34% over the past year and closed at $180.14 on 2026-09-28, still below its $200.89 52-week high, so I am not buying an exhausted move. E&P operating leverage cuts hard if a ceasefire arrives, hence the wider 20% stop and the smaller 8% size next to XLE's 20%.

Trimmed from 10% to 6% as the lower-volatility half of a hard-asset sleeve I no longer want at full size. Bullion rather than miners is the right place for the residual because if the Fed keeps hiking I want the leg that loses 5% rather than the one that loses 7% in the same week. Retained at all because the position hedges the specific scenario my energy overweight cannot survive, namely a Middle East escalation severe enough to be a growth shock rather than just an oil price shock.

Held flat at 6% as the industrial expression of broadening: reshoring, grid and electrical capex, and defense demand that a re-escalating Gulf conflict reinforces. Kept small rather than grown because crude near $95 is a direct input-cost and freight headwind for much of the sector, so industrials are partly on the wrong side of my own largest position. That internal tension is why this stays a minor leg.

The anti-concentration tail, held at 4% and the only leg that made money last week at +0.67%. The Mag7 basket is up roughly 10% from the start of September while the average stock is down roughly 10% from its highs, a divergence the street is openly comparing to 1999-2000. With the 10y at 5.24% the discount rate on the longest-duration equities in the market is the highest in two decades. I keep this deliberately small because this exact short has been the widow-maker of the past year and because a 1.55% SPY rally stopped out four short legs across the desk on entry day last week; 4% with a 10% stop is a position sized to survive being early rather than one sized to be right.
